type: partial versus uniform rescaling, and a new mixed-scale check

the_clean_contrast.reading: scaling itself is not the problem; a single column holding two scales is

new_check.name: MIXED_SCALE
new_check.criterion: continuous positive column with two clusters at least 2 decades apart, each at least 5 percent
new_check.validated: constructed 30 percent rescale flags at 2.8 decades, clean column passes
new_check.scope_note: this project's features are integer codes, so the check cannot fire on the current data; it is prepared for concentration-type features

it_corrects_R153s_closing_judgement: R153 said that if partial scaling also did not matter, scaling could be struck off the list. It does matter and severely, so the correct split is: uniform scaling struck off, partial scaling added
limits: Two scale factors, one fraction, evaluation side only.
The new check only covers magnitude-type unit mixing.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim.
next_gate: generalise MIXED_SCALE from log-space gaps to any bimodality that is separated by a gap, under any monotone scale
